raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, and with only 1.7 mu of summer maize, I won’t do anything fancy. What I know is this: if I miss the season or save too much on fertilizer, the ears come out small and there’s no making it back later. I’ve seen that enough times on my own land and other people’s land. I’m middle-school educated, so I do listen to what the township people say, but in the end I still farm by what has worked here. Since some people in my family work off-farm, labor at home is tight, so I want the work simple and on time. I have well water, so if the rain is short I can still keep the crop going, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate unless the field is really dry at the key stages. I’ll plant summer maize in the usual local window, use a hybrid seed people around here trust, put most fertilizer down early, then add a bit more if the seedlings look weak. I’d rather spend a bit more on enough fertilizer than lose yield by being too stingy, but with such a small plot I still keep the cash spending careful and round-numbered.
